newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Nov 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Nov 19.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- BORROWING BOOST FOR CLARKE

Figures from the British treasury reveal that during October the government collected 4.4 billion stg more in tax revenue than it spent. The figure came as a surprise to economists and forced the government into denying that it signalled wider scope for tax cuts in the forthcoming budget. The data also indicates that chancellor Kenneth Clarke may be on target to hit a year-end target of 26.9 billion stg for overall government borrowing.
-- TELEKOM SHARES SURGE IN BUYING FRENZY

Shares in Deutsche Telekom went on sale to the public on Monday amid strong market demand. Issued at a price of DM28.50 the shares closed some 19 per cent higher at DM33.90, with some 60 million shares in the company being traded within hours of the flotation. The German finance minister hailed the success of the issue as an indication that the general public in his country was shifting in its traditional antipathy towards share ownership.
-- THORN SHARES SLIDE 10 PER CENT ON US WORRIES

Shares in Thorn declined in value by 10 per cent on Monday amid concerns about a range of trading issues, including the prospects for the company's US operations. The concerns overshadowed the announcement of an 11 per cent increase in the recently-demerged company's pre-tax profits to 79.3 million stg. The company warned that trading in the US would next year be extremely tough given the high level of competition.
-- TUC TO SNUB BLAIR WITH CALL FOR EARLIEST ENTRY INTO EMU

In a speech to be delivered to the Federal Trust think-tank on Tuesday the general secretary of the Trades Union Congress, John Monks, will call on the Labour party to commit Britain to early and full participation in the process of Emu. What is expected to be a controversial speech will open a gulf between the TUC and Labour on the issue in the wake of the latter's shift in favour of a referendum on UK participation in the single currency.
-- GILTS PLAN TO ATTRACT FOREIGN BUYERS REVAMPED

The government, in response to pressure from the City, is introducing a range of measures aimed at boosting the attractiveness of UK gilts to foreign investors. Certain overseas investors in government bonds are to be exempt from paying tax on the interest payments received from such investments. The Inland Revenue has noted that the reforms will lead only to a small decline in tax revenue. The changes will be introduced during 1997.
-- BARINGS' FALL 'HAS LED TO BETTER BANK SUPERVISION'

The Governor of the Bank of England, Eddie George, speaking before a Commons treasury select committee, has stated that since the collapse of Barings the system for supervision of banks in the UK has improved markedly. There has also been an improvement in the level of cooperation between regulators in this field in Britain and overseas. However, he cautioned that there was no guarantee as such that such measures would prevent any future collapses.
-- NORTHERN ELECTRIC REJECTS MMC ROLE IN CALENERGY BID

Northern Electric, fighting a hostile takeover bid from US power group CalEnergy, has announced that it sees no role for the Monopolies & Mergers Commission in the bid. The company's chairman, David Morris, noted that the bid would be decided on value alone and that the Northern Electric had no intention of hiding behind an MMC referral. In a letter to shareholders the company has once more rejected the CalEnergy offer as being far too low for consideration.
-- LABOUR PLAN TO FORCE RISE IN WATER INDUSTRY SPENDING

The Labour party will on Tuesday reveal plans to oblige water companies to increase their levels of capital investment. The party has highlighted the lack of progress that has been made in upgrading the country's system of sewers and water mains, many of which were laid in the last century. Privatized water companies are also to face mandatory targets for reducing leakage from their pipe networks.
-- PANIC BUYING CONTRIBUTES TO HOUSE PRICE INCREASES

According to the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors the recent increases in average UK house prices have to some degree been the result of panic buying by investors concerned about missing out on the rewards of a mini-boom. Sellers have also holding back on property sales in the expectation of higher prices, creating a shortage of available stock. The RICS has warned the chancellor Kenneth Clarke against taking steps in his forthcoming Budget that would stimulate an overheated market.
-- POWER CHIEF DENIES INSIDER DEALING CHARGES

The corporate strategy director of Eastern Electricity, Dr Douglas Swinden, has denied charges laid against him in a London court that he purchased shares in another electricity company after making use of confidential information. It has been claimed that the shares were purchased after Swinden learnt that the industry regulator was to ease proposed restrictions on the electricity sector - a decision that led to a rise in electricity share prices.
